conventions: TypeScript strict; Prettier 2.6 via @excalidraw/prettier-config (80 columns, double quotes, trailing commas, semicolons); eslint runs with --max-warnings=0.

Import order (eslint import/order): external packages, then @excalidraw/* packages, then a blank line, then type-only imports (`import type`) in their own group, then parent/sibling relative imports; type imports use `import type`, never inline `type` specifiers.
Inside an import's braces keep the existing case-insensitive alphabetical order (e.g. `EVENT, KEYS, revertDarkModeFilter, rgbToHex, THEME`).

Tests run under vitest 3 with globals (describe/it/expect/vi are global, never imported); assertions use expect(...).toBe / toBeLessThanOrEqual; editor tests render <Excalidraw /> with ./test-utils `render` and read state through `const { h } = window;`.
Every colour helper in packages/common/src/colors.ts returns lowercase hex built with rgbToHex (6 chars when opaque, 8 chars with alpha otherwise).
Do not touch applyDarkModeFilter, cssInvert, cssHueRotate or DARK_MODE_COLORS_CACHE: the dark-mode render path stays byte-identical.
Never run or require `yarn test:update`; no snapshot file changes.

decisions.topic: Name and signature of the inverse
decisions.choice: export const revertDarkModeFilter = (color: string): string in packages/common/src/colors.ts, placed directly after applyDarkModeFilter, re-exported through the existing `export * from "./colors"` in @excalidraw/common.
decisions.reason: A separate pure function keeps the forward path and its cache untouched and matches the requirements' suggested name.

decisions.choice: Undo hue-rotate(180deg) with the same matrix (it equals 2L - I where L is the luminance projection with weights 0.213/0.715/0.072 summing to 1, so it is its own inverse; sin(180deg) terms are ~1e-16), computed unrounded as y = 0.213r + 0.715g + 0.072b and v = 2y - channel; then undo invert(93%) per channel as x = (237.15 - v) / 0.86; clamp x to [0,255] and round once at the end.
rejected: calling cssHueRotate(…, 180) again (it rounds and clamps mid-way, which pushes worst-case error past ±2)
decisions.reason: Closed form is exact for the unclamped case, single final rounding keeps the round-trip error within ±2 per channel (worst case ~1.83 before rounding).

decisions.choice: No cache for revertDarkModeFilter; never read or write DARK_MODE_COLORS_CACHE from it.
decisions.reason: The function is a handful of arithmetic ops per pointer move; the shared cache maps light->dark and must not be polluted with dark->light entries.

decisions.topic: Where the eyedropper maps the colour back
decisions.choice: EyeDropper.tsx keeps getCurrentColor returning the raw sampled hex (used for the preview swatch) and adds a local getPickedColor(color) inside the same useEffect that returns revertDarkModeFilter(color) when appState.theme === THEME.DARK, else color; only the onChange and onSelect arguments go through getPickedColor; appState.theme is added to the effect's dependency array.
rejected: mapping inside getCurrentColor (would change the preview swatch, violating FR-3)
mapping in LayerUI/App callbacks (outside the allowlist and duplicated across three call paths)
decisions.reason: One choke point covers the stroke/background picker, the `i` hotkey and the bucket-fill temporary eyedropper, while the preview keeps showing what is under the cursor.

decisions.topic: How tests simulate a dark-rendered pixel
decisions.choice: Render <Excalidraw theme={THEME.DARK} … /> (or theme light), open the background eyedropper with Keyboard.keyPress("i"), stub `vi.spyOn(h.app.canvas.getContext("2d")!, "getImageData").mockReturnValue({ data: new Uint8ClampedArray([r, g, b, 255]) } as ImageData)` with the channels of applyDarkModeFilter("#1971c2"), then fire pointerDown and pointerUp on the `.excalidraw-eye-dropper-backdrop` element and assert on h.state.currentItemBackgroundColor.
rejected: asserting on a selected element's backgroundColor (needs element setup with no extra coverage)
decisions.reason: vitest-canvas-mock caches one 2D context per canvas, so the stub is the same ctx EyeDropper reads; with no selection App's onSelect writes currentItemBackgroundColor.

decisions.choice: Each test file defines a local helper that parses #rrggbb[aa] with parseInt(hex.slice(i, i + 2), 16) and asserts Math.abs(actual - expected) <= 2 for each of r, g, b.
rejected: exact string equality for dark-theme results
decisions.reason: The round-trip of #1971c2 yields #1971c3, so exact equality is wrong by design; a tiny local parser needs no new import.

units.behaviour: Reproduces the bug: in dark theme the eyedropper writes the on-screen dark-rendered colour instead of the element's real colour; also pins light-theme behaviour.
rules: 1. Add `import { applyDarkModeFilter, THEME } from "@excalidraw/common";` as its own line after the react import, separated by a blank line (external group, @excalidraw after).

2. After the imports add `const { h } = window;` and a local helper `expectHexWithin(actual: string, expected: string, tolerance = 2)` that parses r, g, b with parseInt(hex.slice(i, i + 2), 16) for i = 1, 3, 5 and asserts Math.abs(actual - expected) <= tolerance per channel with expect(...).toBeLessThanOrEqual.

3. Add a local helper `hexToPixel(hex: string)` returning `new Uint8ClampedArray([r, g, b, 255])` parsed the same way, and a helper `openEyeDropperWithPixel(pixel: Uint8ClampedArray)` that presses `i` via Keyboard.keyPress, awaits waitFor until `.excalidraw-eye-dropper-preview` exists, then calls `vi.spyOn(h.app.canvas.getContext("2d")!, "getImageData").mockReturnValue({ data: pixel } as unknown as ImageData)` and returns `{ preview, backdrop }` (backdrop is `.excalidraw-eye-dropper-backdrop` queried from GlobalTestState.renderResult.container).
4. The real colour under test is `#1971c2` (COLOR_PALETTE.blue[4]); the dark pixel is `hexToPixel(applyDarkModeFilter("#1971c2"))`, never a hardcoded hex.

5. Dark-theme case renders `<Excalidraw autoFocus={true} handleKeyboardGlobally={true} theme={THEME.DARK} />`; it fires `fireEvent.pointerDown(backdrop)`, then `fireEvent.pointerMove(window, { clientX: 10, clientY: 10 })` and checks h.state.currentItemBackgroundColor (onChange path), then `fireEvent.pointerUp(backdrop, { clientX: 10, clientY: 10 })` and checks it again (onSelect path), both with expectHexWithin against `#1971c2`.

6. In the dark-theme case, after the pointerMove, assert the preview still shows the raw dark pixel: `expect([applyDarkModeFilter("#1971c2"), "rgb(r, g, b)" of that pixel]).toContain(preview.style.background)` (jsdom may normalise hex to rgb()).

7. Light-theme case renders without the theme prop, stubs the pixel of `#1971c2` itself, fires pointerDown + pointerUp on the backdrop and asserts `h.state.currentItemBackgroundColor` toBe exactly `#1971c2`.
8. Keep the existing `keeps the color preview within the editor container` case byte-identical; new cases go inside the same `describe("eye dropper")` block after it.

units.behaviour: Adds revertDarkModeFilter, the inverse of applyDarkModeFilter (invert(93%) then hue-rotate(180deg)), returning hex with alpha handled the same way.
rules: 1. Insert the function directly after applyDarkModeFilter with a one-line JSDoc: maps a dark-mode rendered colour back to its original colour (inverse of applyDarkModeFilter, lossy where the forward transform clamps).
2. Parse with `const tc = tinycolor(color);`, `const alpha = tc.getAlpha();`, `const { r, g, b } = tc.toRgb();`.
3. Undo hue-rotate(180deg) unrounded: `const luma = 0.213 * r + 0.715 * g + 0.072 * b;` and per channel `v = 2 * luma - channel` (the CSS 180deg hue-rotate matrix equals 2L - I, its own inverse).

4. Undo invert(93%) per channel: `x = (255 * 0.93 - v) / (1 - 2 * 0.93)` written with a named const `DARK_MODE_INVERT_PERCENT = 93` used as p = DARK_MODE_INVERT_PERCENT / 100 so the formula reads (v - 255 * p) / (1 - 2 * p).
5. Round once at the end: `Math.round(clamp(x, 0, 255))` per channel; return `rgbToHex(r, g, b, alpha)` so full opacity yields 6 chars and other alpha yields 8.
6. Pure function: no cache, never touch DARK_MODE_COLORS_CACHE, cssInvert, cssHueRotate or applyDarkModeFilter (the literal 93 in applyDarkModeFilter stays as is).

rules: 1. Extend the @excalidraw/common import to `EVENT, KEYS, revertDarkModeFilter, rgbToHex, THEME` (Prettier wraps it to multiple lines).

2. Right after getCurrentColor, inside the same useEffect, add `const getPickedColor = (color: string) => appState.theme === THEME.DARK ? revertDarkModeFilter(color) : color;` with a short comment that the canvas renders through the dark-mode filter so the sampled pixel must be mapped back.
3. In mouseMoveListener pass `getPickedColor(currentColor)` to stableProps.onChange; leave `colorPreviewDiv.style.background = currentColor;` unchanged.
4. In pointerUpListener call `onSelect(getPickedColor(getCurrentColor(event)), event);`.
5. Add `appState.theme` to the useEffect dependency array after `appState.offsetTop`.
